correctness.rationale: Independently expanded the trace: the diagonal-square cross term contributes 2t²(1−t)² times the adjacent products, the two opposite degree-two shifts contribute the same again, and all nonzero net displacements (±2 and ±4 modulo 5) have zero trace. On the simplex tangent space the first sign change is in modes 2 and 3 at q=1/cos(π/5), with no other zero modes; this proves the entire critical polygon. Above the threshold the same negative tangent eigenvalue occurs on the full support and the zero-sum last sine mode of any induced four-vertex path. The three-point path lower bound is 1/2+(q−1)y+(3/2−q)y² ≥ 1/2, with equality only when the middle mass is zero and the endpoints are equal. On the other three-point face, completing the square in the isolated mass z gives z=(2+q)/(6+q) and the remaining term (2−q)(a−b)²/4. Every support of size at most two is contained in one of these faces. Thus all the listed equality sets, arbitrary phases and both endpoints follow. The equal-q choices of t on line 42 are complementary (their odds are reciprocal); the word 'reciprocal' applied to t itself is an editorial slip, not a different transition parameter.
residual_risks: The auxiliary finite floating-point checks are not used as proof; the result is only for the stated normalized five-cycle problem.

value.rationale: This is a natural normalized extremal problem on the smallest simple odd cycle with a nonadjacent pair and an induced edge plus an isolated vertex. It gives a sharp boundary between uniform and sparse optimizers, including a positive-dimensional critical family and a separate endpoint degeneration. The transition and equality geometry are not supplied by the endpoint value or by a Fourier stability test alone.
residual_risks: The result is a finite-cycle classification, not a theorem for all odd cycles or a quantitative stability analysis.
